item.text: {"classifications":[{"segment_id":"1","code":1,"rationale":"The President directs the Administrator’s future exercise of personnel-management authority, including limits and policies for appointments; any appointment occurs later through agency action, and the provision chiefly governs internal staffing.","evidence":"shall be exercised by the Administrator in accordance with the regulations set forth in this part"},{"segment_id":"2","code":1,"rationale":"The President prescribes internal appointment procedures, certification, disclosure, delegation, and treatment of agency personnel actions; the Administrator and related officials implement these requirements as executive-branch housekeeping.","evidence":"shall be supported by written certification by the Administrator"},{"segment_id":"3","code":1,"rationale":"The Civil Service Commission Chairman must periodically review appointments, report findings, and make recommendations; this creates an internal oversight and reporting process without itself changing legal rights.","evidence":"shall survey appointments made under this part and shall report his findings to the President"},{"segment_id":"4","code":3,"rationale":"The President presently exempts covered appointees from specified federal statutory provisions, subject to stated exceptions; that exemption immediately changes their legal obligations, while the later discretionary authority provisions do not displace this self-executing effect.","evidence":"is hereby exempted, with respect to such employment, from the operation of sections 281, 283, 284, 434, and 1914 of Title 18, United States Code"}]}
